title: Takara Dudley:
title_short: Takara Dudley · AYH · Treat One Another Well
headline: A school district manager who serves homeless students says a brand-new pair of shoes builds confidence, and that there is more happiness in giving.
story: Takara manages the Homeless and Highly Mobile Department at Minneapolis Public Schools. Asked if she is happy, she says yes: the kids, the families, the music, it's a good day.

Many donations her department gets are used. A brand-new pair, fresh out of the box with that new smell, builds confidence. Any time you can give to others, there's more happiness in giving. And you can't get on the bus or go to school without shoes.
Her message is short: treat one another well.

[00:24.5] Volunteer today, but we're partners with Soles4Souls, yes. [do not use: crew set-up talk]
[00:27.6] Minneapolis Public Schools. [do not use: crew set-up talk]

[00:33.5] Sure. [do not use: crew set-up talk]
[00:36.3] So, Takara, would you just...oh, and that's the other thing. [do not use: crew set-up talk]

[00:42.0] Okay. [do not use: crew set-up talk]

[00:46.9] Q: Alright, can you tell me your name and your role? [do not use: crew set-up talk]
[00:49.9] Yes, my name is Takara Dudley and I am the manager of the Homeless and Highly Mobile Department for Minneapolis Public Schools.
[00:56.9] Awesome.
[01:31.1] So, we are here today with Soles4Souls at the Mall of America here in Minnesota, and we are giving away shoes to a variety of different students.
[01:42.6] There are students here from St.
[01:44.2] Paul Public Schools, there are students here from charter schools, and then the district that I work for, Minneapolis Public Schools.
[01:52.6] Q: So, why are we here at the Mall of America with this event?
[01:59.1] Well, last year was the first year that we had an opportunity to partner with Soles4Souls in this way.
[02:04.1] They've been a partner of ours in Minneapolis Public Schools for the last three years, where they've donated shoes to our specific district, to students experiencing homelessness, but this was an opportunity to kind of expand and have them be seen on a wider stage.
[02:20.1] It was really successful last year, so it's been really exciting to see them come back, see the kids, see the parents, see them try on their shoes right then and there, and be able to walk out with them the same day.
[02:32.0] It's just been a really fun event.
[02:34.1] A lot of smiles today.
[02:44.3] I think it changes their confidence.
[02:47.0] There's a lot of things going on in these little people's lives, especially if they are experiencing homelessness, but to have something new, we get quite a few donations in our department, working for Minneapolis Public Schools Homeless and Highly Mobile Department.
[03:01.6] Unfortunately, a lot of this stuff is used.
[03:04.0] So, to have a brand new pair of shoes, fresh out of the box, that have that new smell, it really does build confidence for the kids, and they walk out feeling super excited and super happy.
[03:32.1] Yeah, I mean, to be able to partner with a number of school districts, a number of charters and different organizations.
[03:39.1] I've seen DSW here today.
[03:40.9] I've seen the Foot Locker store here today.
[03:43.1] I've seen different partners working for different companies and school districts.
[03:47.1] So, outside of just being able to give shoes to a few students, an event like this can actually be a lot wider of a range.
[03:55.3] Older kids, because a lot of the kids in our district that we're giving shoes to, a lot of them are younger, kindergarten through fifth grade, but today I've seen even older kids, middle school and high school, be able to get shoes to, which has been really awesome.
[04:16.4] Yeah, I think just how something as simple as a pair of shoes can be a really good boost of confidence for kids.
[04:26.4] Being able to offer our time on a Saturday morning, we could be anywhere else doing anything else, but to give a little bit of yourself.
[04:33.8] I even brought my own teenager here to help today.
[04:36.8] He's volunteering right now giving shoes in the back, and it's like give of yourself a little bit and it'll come back.
[04:43.5] It'll come back.
[04:50.3] Yeah, this partnership has been really awesome.
[04:52.2] It's been a blessing to be able to give shoes to a variety of our students for the last few years.
[05:00.0] We do a couple of different shoe giveaways.
[05:02.0] We do one in the fall and one in the spring.
[05:05.0] I really like that model that we've developed with Soles4Souls because we get kids shoes at the beginning of the school year.
[05:12.0] Of course, they're going to run those down to the ground, which they should, but then to be able to do another giveaway in the spring, sending kids into the summer with a nice pair of shoes to kind of hold them over has been really cool.
[05:24.2] So that's kind of been my favorite thing about this partnership is being able to offer shoes more than one time a year to our students.
[05:33.4] Let's ask a couple of volunteer questions.
[05:38.4] Sure.
[05:46.9] Let's incorporate the question a little bit.
[05:49.7] So if I say why do you want to be a part of it, you can say, I want to be a part of this.
[05:54.1] Yeah.
[05:54.7] I wanted to be a part of this today because I was here last year and I had an opportunity to see it in action.
[06:01.7] The volunteers running back and forth, the kids trying on the shoes, them getting a fresh pair of socks, taking a picture, and then also seeing families together.
[06:11.7] When we do our shoe giveaways, a lot of times it's just students at their school with maybe the social worker or the teacher, but this is a little bit different because we get to see the whole family unit.
[06:21.0] So the little brothers and sisters are here, the mom and dads are here, uncles and aunts are here.
[06:25.7] So it is nice to be able to do this outside of normal school hours to be able to see everybody together.
[06:31.7] I'm sure you don't get that during the day.
[06:34.9] No, we definitely don't.
[06:36.3] Okay.
[06:37.1] Q: So I know it's early, but is there a moment from today that's already stuck with you?
[06:43.8] Just the first couple of kids that came through the door.
[06:47.3] Yes.
[06:47.8] A moment that stuck with me today, just seeing the first couple of kids come through the door, the first two that sat down and tried on their shoes.
[06:55.3] The one kid, his feet weren't even long enough to touch the floor and his feet were kicking back and forth as he's trying to try on the shoes.
[07:01.6] So that was a moment that stuck out today for sure.
[07:03.9] Just the happy smiles and the face.
[07:05.8] And Dora and Spongebob were here, so that's always exciting.
[07:09.8] So, well, you already kind of mentioned it, but let's dig into that.
[07:17.4] Q: What do you notice on kids' faces when they find their pair?
[07:20.7] Q: When kids find their pair, it's a big smile.
[07:24.6] You know, some of it is a little bit of trial and error.
[07:27.1] Maybe not this color, maybe not this size, but once they get that pair and they're able to either carry them out in a fresh box and bag or put them on when they leave, they definitely smile.
[07:39.6] They're definitely excited.
[07:46.9] Q: Why do shoes matter more than people think?
[07:53.0] Yeah, shoes matter maybe more than people think about.
[07:57.7] You know, just most of us, we have a few pairs near the door and we slip them on and we go, or we may have a whole shoe closet that we may take for granted.
[08:07.7] But a lot of our students who are in stable home situations or having to move a lot may not have a lot of items or things. [do not use: unclear words: stable or unstable home situations]
[08:17.7] And you need shoes to be able to go outside, to go get on the bus, to go to school, and then to come back home.
[08:23.7] You can't do that without shoes.
[08:25.8] It's a small thing that people may take for granted, but it is super important that they have shoes that fit them, that feel good, and that look good.
[08:33.2] You look good, you feel good.
[08:39.4] Q: What would you tell someone thinking?
[08:46.2] Yeah, no, this organization is really awesome.
[08:49.2] We had a couple of our school partners in other districts reach out to us when they were thinking about partnering with Soles4Souls, asked us questions.
[08:58.5] Q: How's it going?
[08:59.7] Q: How do you all manage it?
[09:01.2] Q: What's it like working with them?
[09:03.2] We were able to give them some really good feedback, and now we have other school districts in the neighboring area that are partnering with Soles4Souls now.
[09:10.7] So that's been really great.
[09:12.2] So, awesome organization.
[09:14.2] They make it really easy on us.
[09:16.2] We don't have to do a lot of the heavy lifting.
[09:18.2] They kind of make it as seamless as possible because they know we're busy on the school district level.
[09:23.2] So working with them has been awesome, really, really fun.
--- 030_3157.MXF ---
[00:05.0] Am I happy?
[00:07.5] Yeah!
[00:14.7] Just being here today, being with the kids, being with the families, the music is going, it's a good day.
[00:21.7] It's a good day.
[00:30.4] Just that any time that you can give to others, you know, there's more happiness in giving than in receiving, so being able to to step outside of our normal roles on the school level and do something a little different, a little fun, see our kids in a different setting has been really awesome.
[00:47.9] And yeah, a lot of happiness today, a lot of smiles, a lot of laughs.
[00:59.4] Treat one another well.
[01:01.4] That's what I would say.
[01:02.4] If I can give one message, it'd be treat one another well.
